extraction.name: ChartQA
extraction.description: A large-scale benchmark covering 9.6K human-written questions as well as 23.1K questions generated from human-written chart summaries.
extraction.creator: Ahmed Masry, Do Xuan Long, Jia Qing Tan, Shafiq Joty, Enamul Hoque
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Charts were crawled from four online sources, and QA pairs were collected via human annotation and machine generation.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Charts from Statista, Pew research, Our World In Data, and OECD.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Invalid questions were filtered out if the answer could not be found in the chart data table, and the test set was manually cleaned.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowdworkers were asked to write compositional and visual questions for each chart, providing two questions with answers, which were then answered by another annotator.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Answers were checked for exact matches between two workers; disagreements were manually resolved.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The models could potentially be abused to mislead the public.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The models' outputs are not guaranteed to be correct all the time.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and evaluating Chart Question Answering systems.

name.evidence: ChartQA: A Benchmark for Question Answering about Charts with Visual and Logical Reasoning

description.evidence: we present a large-scale benchmark covering 9.6K human-written questions as well as 23.1K questions generated from human-written chart summaries.

url.evidence: Our code and dataset are publicly available at https://github.com/vis-nlp/ChartQA

creator.evidence: Ahmed Masryº, Do Xuan Long¹, Jia Qing Tan¹, Shafiq Joty¹¶, Enamul Hoqueº

rai:dataCollection.evidence: we crawled charts from four different sources: (i) Statista... (ii) The Pew research... (iii) Our World In Data... (iv) Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: we crawled charts from four different sources

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: we crawled charts from four different sources: (i) Statista... (ii) The Pew research... (iii) Our World In Data... (iv) Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: we filter out the question if the answer cannot be found in the chart data table. ... we manually cleaned the test set of the machine generated dataset by removing invalid questions.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: we asked the crowdworkers to focus on two types of questions for each chart image: compositional and visual questions. ... For each chart, the workers provide two questions with the answers. The same questions are then answered by another annotator.

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: collect human-authored QA pairs using Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT)

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: If both workers’ answers exactly match, we consider the answer to be correct. Otherwise, we manually check the answers to select the final correct answer.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: The same questions are then answered by another annotator.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: generated another 23,111 questions automatically from human-written chart summaries using a T5 model

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: Our models can be abused to mislead the public about the charts content and implications.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: we can not guarantee that their output will be correct all the time.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: The goal of a Chart Question Answering (ChartQA) system is to help users by taking a chart and a natural language question as input and predicting the answer.
